 Judgment
Challenging order dated 24.01.2019 passed by 2nd Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bidar (for short 'Commissioner') in ECA no.28/2015, this appeal is filed.
2. Shri.
Sudarshan M., learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by insurer challenging order on ground of violation of terms and conditions of policy and therefore, on liability.

It was submitted that since appeal was filed on ground of liability, finding of NC: 2023:KHC-K:7394 Commissioner regarding relationship of employer and employee, occurrence of incident during course of and out of employment were not in dispute.

It was submitted that as on date of incident i.e., 21.10.2014, Ex.D3 - Driving licence particulars issued by RTA, Bhalki would indicate that driver Vijaykumar S/o Kamanna was having driving licence to drive light motor vehicle valid from 14.02.2001.

However, accident involved heavy goods vehicle and driver was not having valid and The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Vijaykumar And Anr on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172705741/

sentences.text: 2 effective driving licence.
Consequently, there was violation of terms and conditions of policy, which entitled insurer for discharge from liability.
It was submitted that since there was no proper appreciation of evidence by Commissioner, substantial question of law arose for consideration and sought for allowing appeal.
3. On other hand, Shri.Basavaraj R. Math, learned counsel for respondent no.1-claimant sought to support impugned order.

It was submitted that before Commissioner, claimant had produced Ex.P7-endorsement NC: 2023:KHC-K:7394 issued by R.T.A., Basavakalyan, which indicated that licence no.1335/2001 Blk /2001 was issued for driving heavy goods vehicle from 22.12.2011 to 21.12.2014.

Said endorsement would establish that driver had obtained driving licence in respect of heavy goods vehicle from Basavakalyan and therefore, Ex.D3 issued by R.T.A., Bhalki cannot be considered as conclusive.
Therefore, conclusion arrived at by Commissioner was justified.

4. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned order.
5.
It is seen that respondent no.2-employer has filed I.A.1/2023 for production of additional evidence under Order 41, Rule 27 of CPC.

Along with application, certified copy of original endorsement issued by R.T.A., Basavakalyan dated 05.05.2022 is produced, which indicates that driving licence no.1335/2001 Blk/2001 was issued in name of Vijaykumar S/o Kamanna authorizing him to drive heavy transport vehicle from 22.12.2011 to NC: 2023:KHC-K:7394 21.12.2014.
Endorsement is issued specifically for production in this appeal.
In view of above material, it cannot be held that finding of Commissioner regarding liability of insurer was contrary to evidence on record or perverse.
Therefore, no substantial question of law arises for consideration.
Accordingly, appeal is dismissed.
Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Commissioner for disbursement.
In view of disposal of appeal, I.A.1/2023 is dismissed as unnecessary.
